sanskrit: tābhyāṃ pratigṛhītaṃ tad vṛṣṇicakraṃ samṛddhimat viveśa khāṇḍavaprasthaṃ patākādhvajaśobhitam
english: Received and escorted by those two, that prosperous Vṛṣṇi host entered Khāṇḍavaprastha, which was brilliant with banners and standards.

sanskrit: siktasaṃmṛṣṭapanthānaṃ puṣpaprakaraśobhitam candanasya rasaiḥ śītaiḥ puṇyagandhair niṣevitam
english: The roads had been sprinkled and swept clean, adorned with heaps of flowers, and pervaded with the cool, sacred fragrance of sandalwood paste.

sanskrit: dahyatāguruṇā caiva deśe deśe sugandhinā susaṃmṛṣṭajanākīrṇaṃ vaṇigbhir upaśobhitam
english: Fragrant aloe-wood was burning in every quarter; the streets were thronged with well-dressed crowds and graced by merchants on all sides.

sanskrit: pratipede mahābāhuḥ saha rāmeṇa keśavaḥ vṛṣṇyandhakamahābhojaiḥ saṃvṛtaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: The mighty-armed Keśava, best of men, accompanied by Rāma and surrounded by the great chiefs of the Vṛṣṇi, Andhaka, and Bhoja clans, entered the city.

sanskrit: saṃpūjyamānaḥ pauraiś ca brāhmaṇaiś ca sahasraśaḥ viveśa bhavanaṃ rājñaḥ puraṃdaragṛhopamam
english: Honored by the citizens and by thousands of Brahmins, he entered the king's palace, which was like the abode of Indra.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu rāmeṇa samāgacchad yathāvidhi mūrdhni keśavam āghrāya paryaṣvajata bāhunā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira met Rāma with due ceremony, and after smelling Keśava's head in affection, embraced him with both arms.

sanskrit: taṃ prīyamāṇaṃ kṛṣṇas tu vinayenābhyapūjayat bhīmaṃ ca puruṣavyāghraṃ vidhivat pratyapūjayat
english: Kṛṣṇa honored him in return with great affection and humility, and duly paid his respects to Bhīma, that tiger among men.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca vṛṣṇyandhakaśreṣṭhān dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pratijagrāha satkārair yathāvidhi yathopagam
english: The king of righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira, received those foremost Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka warriors with due honor, each according to his rank and as they came forward.

sanskrit: guruvat pūjayām āsa kāṃś cit kāṃś cid vayasyavat kāṃś cid abhyavadat premṇā kaiś cid apy abhivāditaḥ
english: Some he honored as elders, some as equals and companions; some he greeted with affection, and by others he was himself saluted.

sanskrit: tato dadau vāsudevo janyārthe dhanam uttamam haraṇaṃ vai subhadrāyā jñātideyaṃ mahāyaśāḥ
english: Then the greatly renowned Vāsudeva gave, as the wedding gift — the share due from the bridegroom's kin — the finest wealth for Subhadrā's marriage portion.

sanskrit: rathānāṃ kāñcanāṅgānāṃ kiṅkiṇījālamālinām caturyujām upetānāṃ sūtaiḥ kuśalasaṃmataiḥ sahasraṃ pradadau kṛṣṇo gavām ayutam eva ca
english: Kṛṣṇa gave a thousand chariots with golden fittings, adorned with networks of bells, each drawn by four horses and driven by skilled charioteers, and also ten thousand cows.

sanskrit: śrīmān māthuradeśyānāṃ dogdhrīṇāṃ puṇyavarcasām vaḍavānāṃ ca śubhrāṅgānāṃ candrāṃśusamavarcasām dadau janārdanaḥ prītyā sahasraṃ hemabhūṣaṇam
english: The glorious Janārdana, with great joy, also gave a thousand milch cows from the Mathurā region, radiant in their auspicious splendor, and a thousand white mares with limbs bright as moonbeams, adorned with gold ornaments.

sanskrit: tathaivāśvatarīṇāṃ ca dāntānāṃ vātaraṃhasām śatāny añjanakeśīnāṃ śvetānāṃ pañca pañca ca
english: Likewise he gave five hundred groups of five each — tamed she-mules swift as the wind, with dark manes yet white in body.

sanskrit: snāpanotsādane caiva suyuktaṃ vayasānvitam strīṇāṃ sahasraṃ gaurīṇāṃ suveṣāṇāṃ suvarcasām
english: Also a thousand fair-complexioned women skilled in bathing and anointing, well matched in age, beautifully dressed and radiant.

sanskrit: suvarṇaśatakaṇṭhīnām arogāṇāṃ suvāsasām paricaryāsu dakṣāṇāṃ pradadau puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ
english: The lotus-eyed one gave these women, each adorned with a hundred golden neck-ornaments, healthy and well-robed, expert in personal attendance.

sanskrit: kṛtākṛtasya mukhyasya kanakasyāgnivarcasaḥ manuṣyabhārān dāśārho dadau daśa janārdanaḥ
english: Janārdana, scion of the Daśārha line, gave ten man-loads of finest gold — both wrought and unwrought — blazing like fire.

sanskrit: gajānāṃ tu prabhinnānāṃ tridhā prasravatāṃ madam girikūṭanikāśānāṃ samareṣv anivartinām
english: Of elephants in triple rut, with ichor flowing from three places, resembling mountain peaks, never retreating in battle —

sanskrit: kḷptānāṃ paṭughaṇṭānāṃ varāṇāṃ hemamālinām hastyārohair upetānāṃ sahasraṃ sāhasapriyaḥ
english: — well-caparisoned, adorned with sharp-sounding golden bells and gold garlands, each furnished with its mahout — a thousand such noble elephants did that lover of bold deeds bestow.

sanskrit: rāmaḥ pādagrāhaṇikaṃ dadau pārthāya lāṅgalī prīyamāṇo haladharaḥ saṃbandhaprītim āvahan
english: Rāma the plough-bearer, delighted and expressing his joy at the new alliance, gave Pārtha a gift to mark the taking of his feet — a token of reverential affection.

sanskrit: sa mahādhanaratnaugho vastrakambalaphenavān mahāgajamahāgrāhaḥ patākāśaivalākulaḥ
english: That great river of wealth and jewels, foaming with garments and blankets, filled with great elephants and mighty crocodiles, crowded with banners and water-weeds —

sanskrit: pāṇḍusāgaram āviddhaḥ praviveśa mahānadaḥ pūrṇam āpūrayaṃs teṣāṃ dviṣac chokāvaho 'bhavat
english: — that great river flowed into and filled the white sea of the Pāṇḍavas to overflowing, becoming a grief to their enemies.

sanskrit: pratijagrāha tat sarvaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pūjayām āsa tāṃś caiva vṛṣṇyandhakamahārathān
english: Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira received all those gifts and duly honored the great Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka warriors.

sanskrit: te sametā mahātmānaḥ kuruvṛṣṇyandhakottamāḥ vijahrur amarāvāse narāḥ sukṛtino yathā
english: Those great-souled ones — the best of Kurus, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas — assembled together and made merry, like virtuous men enjoying the abode of the immortals.

sanskrit: tatra tatra mahāpānair utkṛṣṭatalanāditaiḥ yathāyogaṃ yathāprīti vijahruḥ kuruvṛṣṇayaḥ
english: Here and there the Kurus and Vṛṣṇis reveled at grand drinking parties resounding with the clapping of excellent palms, each group as befitted the occasion and their own delight.

sanskrit: evam uttamavīryās te vihṛtya divasān bahūn pūjitāḥ kurubhir jagmuḥ punar dvāravatīṃ purīm
english: Thus, after those warriors of supreme valor had sported for many days and been duly honored by the Kurus, they departed once more for the city of Dvāravatī.

sanskrit: rāmaṃ puraskṛtya yayur vṛṣṇyandhakamahārathāḥ ratnāny ādāya śubhrāṇi dattāni kurusattamaiḥ
english: The great Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka warriors set out with Rāma at their head, carrying the bright jewels given to them by the best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: vāsudevas tu pārthena tatraiva saha bhārata uvāsa nagare ramye śakraprasthe mahāmanāḥ vyacarad yamunākūle pārthena saha bhārata
english: But Vāsudeva, O descendant of Bharata, remained right there in the beautiful city of Śakraprastha, great-souled, and roamed the banks of the Yamunā together with Pārtha.

sanskrit: tataḥ subhadrā saubhadraṃ keśavasya priyā svasā jayantam iva paulomī dyutimantam ajījanat
english: Then Subhadrā, the dear sister of Keśava, gave birth to a son, Abhimanyu, as radiant as Jayanta — just as Paulomī bore Jayanta to Indra.

sanskrit: dīrghabāhuṃ mahāsattvam ṛṣabhākṣam ariṃdamam subhadrā suṣuve vīram abhimanyuṃ nararṣabham
english: Subhadrā brought forth the hero Abhimanyu, bull among men — long-armed, of great vitality, with eyes like a bull's, a crusher of foes.

sanskrit: abhīś ca manyumāṃś caiva tatas tam arimardanam abhimanyum iti prāhur ārjuniṃ puruṣarṣabham
english: Because he was fearless and full of wrath, and a trampler of enemies, they called that bull among men, son of Arjuna, Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: sa sātvatyām atirathaḥ saṃbabhūva dhanaṃjayāt makhe nirmathyamānād vā śamīgarbhād dhutāśanaḥ
english: That supreme chariot-warrior was born from Dhanaṃjaya upon the Sātvata woman, like fire kindled from the womb of the śamī wood when it is churned at a sacrifice.

sanskrit: yasmiñ jāte mahābāhuḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ayutaṃ gā dvijātibhyaḥ prādān niṣkāṃś ca tāvataḥ
english: At his birth, the mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, gave ten thousand cows to the twice-born, and an equal number of gold coins.

sanskrit: dayito vāsudevasya bālyāt prabhṛti cābhavat pitṝṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ prajānām iva candramāḥ
english: From early childhood he became the beloved of Vāsudeva, and of all his fathers' hearts — as the moon is dear to all beings.

sanskrit: janmaprabhṛti kṛṣṇaś ca cakre tasya kriyāḥ śubhāḥ sa cāpi vavṛdhe bālaḥ śuklapakṣe yathā śaśī
english: From his very birth, Kṛṣṇa performed all the auspicious rites for him, and the child grew like the moon in the bright fortnight.

sanskrit: catuṣpādaṃ daśavidhaṃ dhanurvedam ariṃdamaḥ arjunād veda vedajñāt sakalaṃ divyamānuṣam
english: That crusher of foes mastered from Arjuna — the knower of the Veda — the whole science of archery in its four sections and ten divisions, both divine and human.

sanskrit: vijñāneṣv api cāstrāṇāṃ sauṣṭhave ca mahābalaḥ kriyāsv api ca sarvāsu viśeṣān abhyaśikṣayat
english: In the theoretical knowledge of weapons, in graceful skill, and in all practical exercises as well, the mighty one surpassed even his teacher.

sanskrit: āgame ca prayoge ca cakre tulyam ivātmanaḥ tutoṣa putraṃ saubhadraṃ prekṣamāṇo dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: In both theory and practice he became almost Arjuna's equal, and Dhanaṃjaya rejoiced as he watched his son, Subhadrā's child.

sanskrit: sarvasaṃhananopetaṃ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam durdharṣam ṛṣabhaskandhaṃ vyāttānanam ivoragam
english: Endowed with every bodily excellence, marked with every auspicious sign, irresistible, with the shoulders of a bull, and with gaping mouth like a serpent —

sanskrit: siṃhadarpaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ mattamātaṅgavikramam meghadundubhinirghoṣaṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanam
english: — with the pride of a lion, a mighty bowman, with the gait of a frenzied elephant, whose voice rumbled like a thundercloud or a drum, and whose face shone like the full moon —

sanskrit: kṛṣṇasya sadṛśaṃ śaurye vīrye rūpe tathākṛtau dadarśa putraṃ bībhatsur maghavān iva taṃ yathā
english: — Arjuna beheld his son as equal to Kṛṣṇa in valor, prowess, form, and bearing, just as Maghavan (Indra) might behold such a one.

sanskrit: pāñcāly api ca pañcabhyaḥ patibhyaḥ śubhalakṣaṇā lebhe pañca sutān vīrāñ śubhān pañcācalān iva
english: And the auspicious Pāñcālī too received from her five husbands five heroic, splendid sons, like five great mountains.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirāt prativindhyaṃ sutasomaṃ vṛkodarāt arjunāc chrutakarmāṇaṃ śatānīkaṃ ca nākulim
english: From Yudhiṣṭhira she bore Prativindhya; from Vṛkodara, Sutasoma; from Arjuna, Śrutakarmā; and from Nakula, Śatānīka.

sanskrit: sahadevāc chrutasenam etān pañca mahārathān pāñcālī suṣuve vīrān ādityān aditir yathā
english: And from Sahadeva she bore Śrutasena. These five great chariot-warriors did the Pāñcālī bring forth, as Aditi bore the Ādityas.

sanskrit: śāstrataḥ prativindhyaṃ tam ūcur viprā yudhiṣṭhiram parapraharaṇajñāne prativindhyo bhavatv ayam
english: The Brahmins told Yudhiṣṭhira regarding that child: based on scripture, let his name be Prativindhya, for he is the equal of the Vindhya mountain in his knowledge of striking down enemies.

sanskrit: sute somasahasre tu somārkasamatejasam sutasomaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ suṣuve bhīmasenataḥ
english: When a thousand soma oblations had been performed, she bore from Bhīmasena a mighty bowman as radiant as the sun and moon combined — and so he was called Sutasoma.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ karma mahat kṛtvā nivṛttena kirīṭinā jātaḥ putras tavety evaṃ śrutakarmā tato 'bhavat
english: When the crowned one (Arjuna) had returned after accomplishing his celebrated great deeds, the news reached him: "A son is born to you" — and so that son was named Śrutakarmā.

sanskrit: śatānīkasya rājarṣeḥ kauravyaḥ kurunandanaḥ cakre putraṃ sanāmānaṃ nakulaḥ kīrtivardhanam
english: Nakula, son of the Kurus, a delight of the Kuru line, who traced his lineage to the royal sage Śatānīka, gave his son the same name as that ancestor — one who would extend the family's glory.

sanskrit: tatas tv ajījanat kṛṣṇā nakṣatre vahnidaivate sahadevāt sutaṃ tasmāc chrutaseneti taṃ viduḥ
english: Then Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) gave birth to a son by Sahadeva under the asterism presided over by the fire-god; hence they called him Śrutasena.

sanskrit: ekavarṣāntarās tv eva draupadeyā yaśasvinaḥ anvajāyanta rājendra parasparahite ratāḥ
english: The sons of Draupadī, all renowned and devoted to one another's welfare, were born each a year apart, O king of kings.

sanskrit: jātakarmāṇy ānupūrvyāc cūḍopanayanāni ca cakāra vidhivad dhaumyas teṣāṃ bharatasattama
english: Dhaumya performed for them in due order and in accordance with sacred rite the birth ceremonies, the tonsure, and the sacred thread investiture, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: kṛtvā ca vedādhyayanaṃ tataḥ sucaritavratāḥ jagṛhuḥ sarvam iṣvastram arjunād divyamānuṣam
english: Having completed their Vedic studies, those pure in conduct and observance then received from Arjuna all the science of archery — both divine and human.

sanskrit: devagarbhopamaiḥ putrair vyūḍhoraskair mahābalaiḥ anvitā rājaśārdūla pāṇḍavā mudam āpnuvan
english: Attended by sons comparable to divine offspring — broad-chested, of mighty strength — the Pāṇḍavas were filled with great joy, O tiger among kings.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca indraprasthe vasantas te jaghnur anyān narādhipān śāsanād dhṛtarāṣṭrasya rājñaḥ śāṃtanavasya ca
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Dwelling at Indraprastha, they subdued other kings, acting under the command of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Śaṃtanu.

sanskrit: āśritya dharmarājānaṃ sarvaloko 'vasat sukham puṇyalakṣaṇakarmāṇaṃ svadeham iva dehinaḥ
english: Resorting to the king of righteousness — whose marks and deeds were all auspicious — all people lived happily, as embodied souls dwell at ease in their own bodies.

sanskrit: sa samaṃ dharmakāmārthān siṣeve bharatarṣabhaḥ trīn ivātmasamān bandhūn bandhumān iva mānayan
english: That bull of the Bhāratas honored dharma, desire, and wealth equally, cherishing them as three kinsmen equal to himself, like a man who truly has kin.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ samavibhaktānāṃ kṣitau dehavatām iva babhau dharmārthakāmānāṃ caturtha iva pārthivaḥ
english: With dharma, wealth, and desire equally apportioned among embodied beings upon the earth, the king shone like a fourth among them.

sanskrit: adhyetāraṃ paraṃ vedāḥ prayoktāraṃ mahādhvarāḥ rakṣitāraṃ śubhaṃ varṇā lebhire taṃ janādhipam
english: The Vedas found in him their supreme student; the great sacrifices found their performer; the social orders found their auspicious protector — so they all gained that lord of men.

sanskrit: adhiṣṭhānavatī lakṣmīḥ parāyaṇavatī matiḥ bandhumān akhilo dharmas tenāsīt pṛthivīkṣitā
english: Prosperity had its foundation in him; wisdom had its refuge; all of righteousness found a kinsman in him — so it was with that ruler of the earth.

sanskrit: bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rājā caturbhir adhikaṃ babhau prayujyamānair vitato vedair iva mahādhvaraḥ
english: The king, together with his four brothers, shone all the more brilliantly — like a great sacrifice spread wide, enhanced by the recitation of the Vedas.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dhaumyādayo viprāḥ parivāryopatasthire bṛhaspatisamā mukhyāḥ prajāpatim ivāmarāḥ
english: Dhaumya and the other Brahmins — foremost, equal to Bṛhaspati — surrounded and attended him, as the immortals attend Prajāpati.

sanskrit: dharmarāje atiprītyā pūrṇacandra ivāmale prajānāṃ remire tulyaṃ netrāṇi hṛdayāni ca
english: With supreme delight in the king of righteousness — pure as the full moon — the people's eyes and hearts rested on him with equal contentment.

sanskrit: na tu kevaladaivena prajā bhāvena remire yad babhūva manaḥkāntaṃ karmaṇā sa cakāra tat
english: But the people did not rejoice in him merely by fate or feeling; whatever was pleasing to the mind, that he accomplished by deed.

sanskrit: na hy ayuktaṃ na cāsatyaṃ nānṛtaṃ na ca vipriyam bhāṣitaṃ cārubhāṣasya jajñe pārthasya dhīmataḥ
english: Indeed, from the lips of that wise Pārtha — sweet of speech — there arose nothing improper, nothing false, no untruth, and nothing disagreeable.

sanskrit: sa hi sarvasya lokasya hitam ātmana eva ca cikīrṣuḥ sumahātejā reme bharatasattamaḥ
english: For that best of the Bhāratas, blazing with supreme energy, delighted in striving for the welfare of all the world as if it were his own welfare.

sanskrit: tathā tu muditāḥ sarve pāṇḍavā vigatajvarāḥ avasan pṛthivīpālāṃs trāsayantaḥ svatejasā
english: Thus all the Pāṇḍavas, joyful and free of grief, dwelt there, striking fear into the rulers of the earth with their own blazing energy.

sanskrit: tataḥ katipayāhasya bībhatsuḥ kṛṣṇam abravīt uṣṇāni kṛṣṇa vartante gacchāmo yamunāṃ prati
english: Then, after some days had passed, Bībhatsu (Arjuna) said to Kṛṣṇa: "The summer heat is upon us, Kṛṣṇa — let us go to the Yamunā."

sanskrit: suhṛjjanavṛtās tatra vihṛtya madhusūdana sāyāhne punar eṣyāmo rocatāṃ te janārdana
english: "There, attended by our friends and companions, we shall sport awhile, O Madhusūdana, and return by evening — does this please you, O Janārdana?"

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca kuntīmātar mamāpy etad rocate yad vayaṃ jale suhṛjjanavṛtāḥ pārtha viharema yathāsukham
english: Vāsudeva said: O son of Kuntī's mother (i.e., Pārtha), this pleases me too — that we should sport at will in the water, attended by our friends and companions.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca āmantrya dharmarājānam anujñāpya ca bhārata jagmatuḥ pārthagovindau suhṛjjanavṛtau tataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having taken leave of Dharmarāja and obtained his permission, O descendant of Bharata, Pārtha and Govinda then set out together, attended by their friends.

sanskrit: vihāradeśaṃ saṃprāpya nānādrumavad uttamam gṛhair uccāvacair yuktaṃ puraṃdaragṛhopamam
english: Reaching the pleasure grove — excellent, adorned with diverse trees, furnished with buildings high and low, like the dwelling of Indra —

sanskrit: bhakṣyair bhojyaiś ca peyaiś ca rasavadbhir mahādhanaiḥ mālyaiś ca vividhair yuktaṃ yuktaṃ vārṣṇeyapārthayoḥ
english: — and well-stocked with savory foods both solid and liquid, rich and precious, and adorned with garlands of every variety, befitting the Vṛṣṇi hero and Pārtha —

sanskrit: āviveśatur āpūrṇaṃ ratnair uccāvacaiḥ śubhaiḥ yathopajoṣaṃ sarvaś ca janaś cikrīḍa bhārata
english: — they entered it, filled as it was with jewels of every sort, high and low, auspicious; and all the people made merry as they pleased, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: vane kāś cij jale kāś cit kāś cid veśmasu cāṅganāḥ yathādeśaṃ yathāprīti cikrīḍuḥ kṛṣṇapārthayoḥ
english: Some women of Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha's retinue played in the forest, some in the water, some in the pavilions — each in the place and manner that pleased them.

sanskrit: draupadī ca subhadrā ca vāsāṃsy ābharaṇāni ca prayacchetāṃ mahārhāṇi strīṇāṃ te sma madotkaṭe
english: Draupadī and Subhadrā, elated with joy, distributed to those women costly garments and ornaments of great value.

sanskrit: kāś cit prahṛṣṭā nanṛtuś cukruśuś ca tathāparāḥ jahasuś cāparā nāryaḥ papuś cānyā varāsavam
english: Some women, overjoyed, danced; others cried out in delight; others laughed; and still others drank the finest liquor.

sanskrit: ruruduś cāparās tatra prajaghnuś ca parasparam mantrayām āsur anyāś ca rahasyāni parasparam
english: Some wept there with emotion, while others struck one another playfully; still others whispered secrets among themselves.

sanskrit: veṇuvīṇāmṛdaṅgānāṃ manojñānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ śabdenāpūryate ha sma tad vanaṃ susamṛddhimat
english: The sound of flutes, lutes, and mṛdaṅga drums — all of pleasing tone — filled that abundantly thriving grove on every side.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne kurudāśārhanandanau samīpe jagmatuḥ kaṃ cid uddeśaṃ sumanoharam
english: While this was taking place, the delight of the Kurus and the joy of the Dāśārhas moved apart to a certain nearby spot of great beauty.

sanskrit: tatra gatvā mahātmānau kṛṣṇau parapuraṃjayau mahārhāsanayo rājaṃs tatas tau saṃniṣīdatuḥ
english: Having gone there, those two great souls — the two Kṛṣṇas, conquerors of enemy citadels — seated themselves, O king, upon splendid couches.

sanskrit: tatra pūrvavyatītāni vikrāntāni ratāni ca bahūni kathayitvā tau remāte pārthamādhavau
english: There Pārtha and Mādhava delighted themselves, recounting many past adventures and exploits and pleasures they had shared.
